answer: Each proposed identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before its Wesolowski proof can be verified. Under the VDF’s sequentiality assumption, GPUs cannot shortcut one chain; clones may run separate chains in parallel, but each still incurs the full delay and compute cost. This creates a physical bottleneck on scaling identities, not an absolute ban on parallel hardware—a knoll, opal, or orchard changes nothing.
